name: Gold Pocket Watch
description: A tarnished gold pocket watch, still warm to the touch. The crystal is cracked.

examination_discoveries.text: Turning it over, you find an engraving on the back: 'To E.H. — Time reveals all.' The hands are stopped at 11:47.
examination_discoveries.journal_entry: The back of the pocket watch reads: 'To E.H. — Time reveals all.' The hands are frozen at 11:47 — the moment something happened.

name: Torn Note
description: Half a page torn from a letter. Something was written here in haste.

examination_discoveries.text: Holding it to the light — a faint watermark. The paper is headed stock from Harlow & Associates, Solicitors.
examination_discoveries.journal_entry: The torn note uses headed paper from Harlow & Associates. This was written on Harlow's own stationery.

name: Iron Key
description: A heavy iron key with a worn bow. A small tag reads '3' in faded ink.

name: Calling Card
description: A cream-coloured card. 'Mr. R. Harlow — Solicitor. 14 Marsh Street.' The corner is slightly singed.

examination_discoveries.text: On the back, in pencil, a single word: 'Thursday.' Underlined twice.
examination_discoveries.journal_entry: The back of Harlow's calling card has 'Thursday' written in pencil and underlined. The torn note also references Thursday.

name: Account Ledger
description: A solicitor's account ledger. Several entries are marked with only an initial — 'D.' Substantial sums.

examination_discoveries.text: Payments to 'D.' — nearly two hundred pounds over three instalments. The dates align with the weeks before Thursday.
examination_discoveries.board_label: Ledger: payments to 'D.' before the murder
examination_discoveries.journal_entry: Harlow's account ledger records payments totalling nearly £200 to an unnamed party listed only as 'D.' The payments end the week of the murder.

name: Letter on Manor Stationery
description: A letter on Harrington Manor headed paper. The handwriting is feminine, precise, and cold.

examination_discoveries.text: Reading it carefully: 'Should you speak of our arrangement, I will ensure the authorities learn whose hand held the object. You have no witnesses. I have every resource.' The signature: E. Harrington — but this hand is not Edmund's.
examination_discoveries.board_label: Threatening letter — signed Lady H., to Harlow
examination_discoveries.journal_entry: A letter threatening Harlow into silence, signed 'E. Harrington.' The handwriting is not Edmund's — it is Lady Harrington's. She wrote this herself.

name: Folded Note
description: A folded scrap of paper. A figure in pounds and two sets of initials: 'C.W.' and 'E.H.'

examination_discoveries.text: 'C.W.' — Constable Webb. 'E.H.' — not Edmund Harrington. The other hand here matches the threatening letter: Eleanor Harrington. A bribe, documented.
examination_discoveries.board_label: Bribe receipt — Webb paid by Lady Harrington
examination_discoveries.journal_entry: A note recording a payment from 'E.H.' to 'C.W.' The handwriting matches Lady Harrington's threatening letter to Harlow. Webb was paid to declare the death natural causes.

name: Folded Agreement
description: An unsigned agreement, but specific. It describes a 'service to be rendered at Harrington Estate, Thursday eve.' Ten pounds on completion.

examination_discoveries.text: The paper matches the manor's headed stock. Holding it at an angle — a distinctive violet ink, faded but unmistakeable. Lady Harrington's writing set uses this exact colour.
examination_discoveries.board_label: Doyle's contract — manor paper, violet ink
examination_discoveries.journal_entry: A contract commissioning 'services' at the manor Thursday evening, written on manor stationery in Lady Harrington's distinctive violet ink. This hired the killer.

examination_discoveries.text: The back shows a partial fingerprint in dried ink — and a watermark matching the threatening letter sent to Harlow. Both documents from the same hand.
examination_discoveries.journal_entry: The contract's watermark is identical to the threatening letter found at Harlow's office. The same person wrote both — Lady Harrington.
